title: Guiding Application Users via Estimation of Computational Resources for Massively Parallel Chemistry Computations
problem: Users struggle to predict resource requirements (nodes, tile sizes, runtime) for expensive chemistry computations on supercomputers, leading to suboptimal submissions and wasted allocations.
motivation: Massively parallel chemistry applications (e.g., CCSD) have complex parameter spaces; users need guidance to minimize execution time or costs before submitting.
method: Machine learning models (Gradient Boosting, Active Learning) to predict CCSD execution time for given problem sizes and parameter values, enabling resource optimization on Frontier and Aurora.
key_novelty: First ML-based resource prediction framework for chemistry applications with cost-optimization strategies; combines GB models with active learning for limited experimental data.
contributions: Active Learning approach: MAPE ~0.2 with only 450 experiments
Predicts optimal node counts and tile sizes for shortest runtime
Validated on CCSD Coupled Cluster application
Deployed on Frontier and Aurora supercomputers
workloads: CCSD (Coupled Cluster with Singles and Doubles)
limitations: Abstract-only; unclear on generalization to other chemistry codes, data collection methodology, or prediction latency
